title: RefSwap: Counterfactual Reference-Swap Verification for Robust LLM Verifiers

contributions.purpose: Expose that reference-based RLVR verifiers can be fooled by trivial 'master-key' responses.
contributions.mechanism: Systematic measurement of false positive rates of master-key attacks (single tokens or short phrases exploiting reference answer leakage) against state-of-the-art verifiers.
contributions.evaluation: Master keys achieve 25-29% false positive verification rates on state-of-the-art verifiers including xVerify and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.
contributions.source_quote: We identify and quantify the master-key vulnerability in RLVR verifiers, showing 25-29% false positive rates on state-of-the-art systems.

contributions.purpose: Detect master-key attacks without any verifier retraining.
contributions.mechanism: Multi-CF RefSwap, a training-free method that samples K counterfactual references and computes the maximum verification probability (max_p_cf), exploiting the self-solving asymmetry between legitimate correct responses and master-key false positives.
contributions.evaluation: Multi-CF RefSwap achieves near-perfect separation between true positives and master keys (AUC=0.991).
contributions.source_quote: We propose Multi-CF RefSwap, a training-free detection method using max_p_cf scoring that exploits the self-solving asymmetry between true positives and master keys.

contributions.purpose: Show the detection method substantially reduces master-key false positives at small accuracy cost.
contributions.mechanism: Applying RefSwap filtering to the xVerify-7B-I verifier across 10 master-key attacks.
contributions.evaluation: 96.8% relative FPR reduction (25.50% to 0.81%) on xVerify-7B-I with only 2.74pp accuracy cost, uniformly neutralizing all 10 tested master keys.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate 96.8% relative FPR reduction (25.50%->0.81%) on xVerify-7B-I with only 2.74pp accuracy cost, uniformly neutralizing all 10 tested master keys.

contributions.purpose: Characterize when counterfactual-based detection works across verifier backbones.
contributions.mechanism: Backbone dependency analysis comparing RefSwap effectiveness on xVerify versus Qwen verifiers.
contributions.evaluation: RefSwap works on xVerify but not Qwen, revealing that verifier architecture/backbone design determines susceptibility to counterfactual-based detection.
contributions.source_quote: We analyze backbone dependency, revealing that verifier architecture determines susceptibility to counterfactual-based detection.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our work extends these robustness concerns to the specific setting of reference-based verification in reinforcement learning.
Our work identifies a fundamental vulnerability in this verification paradigm: the potential for trivial responses to exploit reference answer leakage.
Our master-key attack represents a particularly severe form of reward hacking where trivial responses achieve false positive verification, potentially corrupting the entire training process.

notes: Mixed/partially negative result acknowledged in the abstract and contribution list: RefSwap works on xVerify but fails on Qwen backbones. The master-key attack itself builds on Zhao et al. (2025) reference answer leakage observations.
